title: "A prioritized agenda"
subtitle: "What should change in practice now, what to build next, and what is worth the risk"
toc: true
---

The catalog lists problems. This page ranks them, in three tiers plus a list of work the field
does not need. Tier 1 requires no new methodology: every item is something an analyst could do
differently in the next study. Tiers 2 and 3 are research programs.

The priority field carried on each entry is weak evidence and is treated as such: 10 of the 43
entries are graded Very high and 27 High, which is under half a bit of information. The ranking
below rests on three observable things instead. Whether the problem changes what the estimate
means rather than how precisely it is measured. Whether any method addresses it at all, which
is what the verdict records. And whether anything runnable implements it, which is checked
against the version-pinned source in
[the method landscape](landscape.qmd).

## Tier 1: change current practice now

These need no new theory. Every one is a convention the field could adopt in its next protocol.

1. **Report the estimand you estimated, not the one you set out to estimate.** A hazard ratio
   published where the design targeted a weighted per-protocol effect among the grace-period
   compliers is a different quantity with the same name.
   See [EST-03](problems/EST-03-a-hazard-ratio-is-reported-where-the-estimand-was-a-weighted.qmd).

2. **State the grace period and the time grid before looking at the outcome, and report the
   estimate under at least one other choice.** Both are modeling decisions that move the
   estimand, and neither has an outcome-blind selection procedure.
   See [TZO-01](problems/TZO-01-no-outcome-blind-procedure-selects-the-time-grid-or-the-grac.qmd).

3. **Name which patient histories are unsupported, not how heavy the weights got.** A weight
   distribution is a symptom. The decision-relevant quantity is the fraction of person-time for
   which the assigned strategy was never observed, and the estimate with and without it.
   See [OVL-01](problems/OVL-01-positivity-diagnostics-describe-weights-instead-of-naming-wh.qmd).

4. **Treat censoring at a competing event as an identifying assumption and say which estimand it
   selects.** Censoring at death is currently applied as data cleaning, which chooses a
   counterfactual quantity by default rather than by argument.
   See [OUT-01](problems/OUT-01-censoring-at-death-is-applied-as-data-cleaning-rather-than-a.qmd).

5. **Separate the assumptions that can be diagnosed from those that cannot, and report them
   separately.** An analysis that lists positivity diagnostics beside an assertion of
   exchangeability invites a reader to treat both as checked.
   See [REG-02](problems/REG-02-there-is-no-assumption-dashboard-so-diagnosable-and-undiagno.qmd).

6. **Do not treat the phrase target trial emulation as evidence about the analysis.** The label
   describes a design discipline, not a discharged assumption burden, and it is currently cited
   as though it were the second thing.
   See [REG-03](problems/REG-03-calling-an-analysis-a-target-trial-emulation-is-treated-as-e.qmd).

7. **Publish the phenotype logic, the weight diagnostics and the rejected protocol versions, not
   only the final protocol.** A registration recording only what survived hides the researcher
   degrees of freedom it exists to constrain.
   See [SFW-03](problems/SFW-03-code-phenotype-logic-weight-diagnostics-and-rejected-protoco.qmd)
   and [PRO-03](problems/PRO-03-registrations-record-the-final-protocol-and-not-the-alternat.qmd).

8. **Report benchmarking as a calibrated comparison of estimates, not as agreed or not
   agreed.** A binary replication label mixes estimand mismatch with random error, and it is the
   label that gets cited.
   See [BEN-02](problems/BEN-02-replication-is-reported-as-a-binary-label-rather-than-as-a-c.qmd).

9. **Vary violated assumptions jointly.** Confounding, measurement error and informative visits
   occur together; a one-at-a-time sensitivity analysis can make a cancellation accident look
   like robustness.
   See [UCF-02](problems/UCF-02-sensitivity-analyses-vary-one-violated-assumption-at-a-time-.qmd).

10. **Show that the estimator choice did not decide the answer.** No estimator is defensible as a
    default, and nothing currently requires a study to demonstrate that a different one would
    have agreed.
    See [GMT-04](problems/GMT-04-no-estimator-is-defensible-as-a-default-and-no-study-is-requ.qmd).

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
## The one-page test

A committee-facing summary should answer nine questions. If an analysis cannot, the problem is
not the statistics.

What is being estimated, on what scale, at what horizon? For whom? When is time zero, and do
eligibility, assignment and the start of follow-up coincide there? What is the treatment
strategy, and what grace period makes it achievable? Which variables are assumed to make
treatment as good as randomized at each time point? What fraction of person-time had no support
for the assigned strategy? Which variables are algorithms rather than measurements? Which
assumptions were diagnosed and which were asserted? How much assumption violation changes the
recommendation?
:::

## Tier 2: develop and validate next

Tractable programs where a first publishable contribution is within reach. Everything here is
graded 4 or 5 out of 5 for tractability in the catalog.

- An outcome-blind procedure for selecting the grace period and the time grid, and a reporting
  convention that shows the estimand moving with them
- A positivity account that names unsupported histories and reports the estimate restricted to
  the supported region, in place of weight diagnostics
- Cross-validation criteria for longitudinal nuisance models that target causal error rather
  than predictive error
  ([GMT-01](problems/GMT-01-cross-validation-for-longitudinal-nuisance-models-optimizes-.qmd))
- A scalable and correct default for variance after cloning and sequence expansion
  ([SFW-01](problems/SFW-01-variance-estimation-after-cloning-and-sequence-expansion-has.qmd))
- End-to-end propagation of phenotype misclassification through a longitudinal estimator, rather
  than a validation study reported beside an analysis that assumes error-free variables
  ([MER-01](problems/MER-01-phenotypes-enter-emulations-as-error-free-binary-variables.qmd))
- Thresholds for data fitness that can stop a study, and a route to publishing a negative fitness
  assessment
  ([DTA-01](problems/DTA-01-data-fitness-assessment-is-narrative-and-has-no-thresholds-t.qmd))
- Semantic conformance checking for common data models, so harmonized structure is not mistaken
  for harmonized meaning
  ([DTA-03](problems/DTA-03-common-data-models-harmonize-structure-without-guaranteeing-.qmd))
- Federated diagnostics that surface between-site estimand heterogeneity instead of averaging
  over it
  ([DTA-02](problems/DTA-02-averaging-site-estimates-in-a-federated-emulation-can-concea.qmd))
- Person-clustered and calendar-time-aware inference for sequential nested trials, validated in
  finite samples rather than asymptotically
  ([SEQ-01](problems/SEQ-01-sequential-emulation-creates-repeated-participation-and-cale.qmd))
- Bias bounds for comparator sampling schemes computable before cohort construction
  ([ELG-03](problems/ELG-03-no-procedure-bounds-the-bias-a-comparator-sampling-scheme-in.qmd))
- Verification that automated protocol translation preserves the estimand, not only that it
  produces running code
  ([LRN-02](problems/LRN-02-automated-protocol-translation-can-change-the-estimand-while.qmd))
- Subgroup estimation that reports overlap per subgroup, since the groups with the worst overlap
  are the ones the analysis exists to serve
  ([LRN-04](problems/LRN-04-subgroup-effects-are-estimated-where-overlap-is-worst-and-th.qmd))
- Evaluation of generative models on causal quantities rather than on distributional fidelity
  ([SFW-02](problems/SFW-02-generative-models-are-evaluated-on-distributional-fidelity-a.qmd))
- A discrepancy prior for entering an emulation into a synthesis with randomized trials,
  calibrated on the existing benchmarking literature
  ([EST-05](problems/EST-05-an-emulation-enters-a-synthesis-with-randomized-trials-throu.qmd))

## Tier 3: high risk, high reward

Where the payoff is large and a clean result is not likely. These are the entries the catalog
grades 2 or 3 for tractability, and the ones where the obstacle is identification rather than
engineering.

- Identification of dynamic regimes in continuous time under a treatment-dependent observation
  process, which is the ordinary situation in electronic health records and the one the discrete
  g-formula assumes away
  ([GMT-02](problems/GMT-02-identification-of-dynamic-regimes-in-continuous-time-under-t.qmd))
- Interference and the joint strategies cloning can construct that no policy could implement
  ([EST-01](problems/EST-01-emulation-assumes-no-interference-and-cloning-individuals-ca.qmd))
- The visit process as part of the causal structure rather than as missingness to impute
  ([MIS-01](problems/MIS-01-the-visit-process-is-treated-as-a-nuisance-to-be-imputed-rat.qmd))
- Negative controls, proxies and validation data integrated into one bias account instead of
  three separate reassurances
  ([UCF-01](problems/UCF-01-negative-controls-proxies-and-validation-data-are-not-integr.qmd))
- A mediated estimand defined for a sustained strategy realized by cloning and artificial
  censoring, with a protocol slot that fixes the mediator before the analysis
  ([EST-04](problems/EST-04-no-mediated-effect-is-defined-for-a-sustained-treatment-stra.qmd))
- Clinically defensible equivalence classes of treatment versions, which is what consistency
  quietly assumes
  ([STR-01](problems/STR-01-no-procedure-defines-clinically-defensible-equivalence-class.qmd))
- Inference that accounts for the target trial having been selected after seeing the data
  ([PRO-02](problems/PRO-02-inference-conditions-on-a-fixed-target-trial-that-was-in-fac.qmd))
- Counterfactual prediction validated outside the assumptions that produced it, with operating
  characteristics under exchangeability failure
  ([LRN-05](problems/LRN-05-a-counterfactual-prediction-is-validated-under-the-assumptio.qmd))
- Regulatory thresholds for adequate emulation, acceptable residual confounding and sufficient
  data fitness, which is a governance problem carrying a methodological core
  ([REG-01](problems/REG-01-regulators-have-no-thresholds-for-adequate-emulation-accepta.qmd))
- Emulation of non-pharmaceutical and policy interventions whose treatment versions are not
  enumerable, the one entry in the catalog the auditors could not settle
  ([PRO-05](problems/PRO-05-emulation-is-proposed-for-non-pharmaceutical-and-policy-inte.qmd))

## What the field does not need

Stated plainly, because an agenda that only adds is not an agenda. Each of these is refused for
a reason recorded in the catalog or in the rejected candidates.

- **Another emulation demonstrating that immortal time bias exists.** It is the most-restated
  finding in the entire reading and has been settled since 2008.
- **Another package reimplementing inverse probability weighting under a new function name.**
  The gap named in the catalog is a missing default for variance after cloning, not a missing
  weighting routine.
- **Simulation studies run where every method works.** Correct specification, good overlap,
  measured confounders and complete follow-up describe conditions under which the estimator
  choice cannot matter, which is the question the study was meant to answer.
- **Adopting a more flexible estimator in place of an identification argument.** This is a
  catalogued error, not a research direction
  ([LRN-01](problems/LRN-01-flexible-estimation-is-presented-as-a-remedy-for-identificat.qmd)).
- **Papers observing that applied subfields have not adopted existing methods.** Named
  independently by four gap labellers and rejected on assessment: the sources themselves say the
  methods are available in standard software and simply not used, which is a fact about
  diffusion rather than a gap in the field.
- **Requests for someone to write a package.** Named independently by three labellers, rejected
  twice on the same ground. It closes with engineering and funding, not with research, and the
  methodological residue is already carried by
  [GMT-04](problems/GMT-04-no-estimator-is-defensible-as-a-default-and-no-study-is-requ.qmd)
  and [SFW-03](problems/SFW-03-code-phenotype-logic-weight-diagnostics-and-rejected-protoco.qmd).
- **Reporting checklists that stop where the disputes start.** A guideline covering what to
  report about eligibility and time zero, and nothing about grace periods, cloning or
  time-varying confounding, standardizes the easy half.

## The organizing discipline

> No effect estimate without a stated estimand at a stated horizon. No time zero without
> eligibility, assignment and follow-up aligned at it. No sustained strategy without the grace
> period that makes it achievable and the positivity account that makes it estimable. No
> exchangeability claim without a bias analysis that says how much violation the conclusion
> survives.
